extraction.name: Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models?
extraction.description: This paper evaluates large vision-language models (LVLMs) and identifies issues with current evaluation methods.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves roughly selecting samples from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, and then human review is applied to ensure each curated sample exhibits visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requires advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data collection involves selecting samples from existing benchmarks such as MMMU, MMBench, ScienceQA, AI2D, SEED, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing protocol involves filtering out samples that can be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLM inspectors, and then manual review to ensure visual dependency and minimal data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The data annotation protocol involves human annotation to ensure each curated sample exhibits visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requires advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The data annotation analysis involves calculating the hit frequency for each evaluation sample using LLM inspectors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The limitations of existing benchmarks include lack of visual dependency and unintentional data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The use case of MMStar benchmark is to evaluate the multi-modal capabilities of LVLMs.
